title: PINs to Projects
text: This website documents how individual Property Index Numbers (PINs) were grouped into larger commercial and industrial property projects.

title: PINs to Projects
section: Why reports are organized by township
text:
Why reports are organized by township
The underlying analysis and parcel retrieval are already township-based. Township reports also avoid generating roughly 130 largely repetitive municipality pages. Municipality and PIN lookup tables provide direct paths into the relevant pre-rendered township reports.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
A PIN identifies an individual tax parcel. A single commercial or industrial development may contain several parcels and therefore several PINs.
A project is the broader property grouping created from the available appeal records, sale documents, valuation worksheets, and parcel proximity. The manually assigned key PIN identifies that grouped project.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:

A project is the broader property grouping created from the available appeal records, sale documents, valuation worksheets, and parcel proximity. The manually assigned key PIN identifies that grouped project.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
Geographic organization
Each PIN is associated with a municipality and a township. The detailed reports are rendered by township because the parcel analysis was written around township boundaries and because there are substantially fewer townships than municipalities.
Municipal boundaries and township boundaries do not always match. A municipality may therefore appear in more than one township report. The municipality directory lists every relevant township report rather than pretending each municipality belongs to exactly one township.

title: How PINs Relate to Projects
text:
Using the site
Use Municipalities when you know the municipality name. Use Search PINs when you know a PIN, project key PIN, appellant, township, or municipality. Both pages link to the pre-rendered township reports.
